transcript:
# Municipal Building Committee:
# Malden River Works Salt Shed & Boathouse
# Agenda

| June 17, 2026 | 1PM | Virtual Teams Meeting |
|---|---|---|

https://teams.microsoft.com/meet/26476107111150?p=tcy9yoBIOrkfVDsjS3

Meeting was called to order at 1:09PM.

## Roll Call

- Deborah Burke - Present
- Peg Crowe – Joined after roll call
- Amanda Linehan
- Nelson Miller - Present
- Paul Myers - Present
- Eric Rubin - Present
- Stephen Winslow – Present

## Committee to Approve Minutes

Committee to approve the 5/5/26 and 6/4/26 meeting minutes.

- Eric motioned to approve both sets of minutes. This motion was seconded by Deb, and both sets of minutes were approved unanimously.

## Malden River Works Salt Shed & Boathouse Project Updates

Sustainability & Grants Manager Rebekah McPheeters to provide high level project updates.

- Bekah was on site earlier today. Phase 1 construction is wrapping up now. Everything looks really good, and Nangle especially applauded Phelan for handling the complicated soil contamination work well.

## Cost Estimate Update

designLAB to provide updates regarding the project cost estimates.

- Sam with designLAB (dL) walked through slides for this portion of the meeting. The slides are attached to these minutes.
- Construction cost estimate for both salt shed and boathouse came to $4,168,600
  - Boathouse estimate is $2,471,600
  - Salt shed estimate is $1,697,000
  - These numbers do not include soft costs
  - Sam noted that these seem high, so dL asked for a peer review of the estimates, they are waiting to hear back
- Sam walked through our options for additional cost savings
  - Moving to wood siding saves $2500
  - Roofing material change (to corrugated metal) saves $50,400
  - Window type change saves $3255
    - But this approach is not recommended because it becomes a filed sub bid
  - Conduit to MC cable change saves $37,200
  - Boat racks – We could take them out of the bid and handle them as FFE. This would save $42k now, and maybe about $4,200 (10%) later when we buy them separately
  - Overall, if we approve the savings that dL recommends, we could see savings of $132,100
    - The new construction cost estimate would be $4,036,500
- Additional options
  - We could bid the salt shed as a deduct alternate to possibly get a lower cost
  - We could consider a hoop structure for the salt shed (but note that this would be less durable and would cut down on salt capacity)
    - There may be as much as $1.6M savings here
    - Marie with Landing Studios says she believes all of these options are still compliant, but that we should check on this
- Next Steps
  - dL recommends we make a decision on these options soon, so they can move on to Construction Documents as soon as possible, to avoid cost escalations
  - Committee decided to meet again next week to discuss, and then to follow up with dL via email afterwards with decisions
    - Meeting scheduled for Thursday, June 25 at 2PM
    - Deb asked that Ron Hogan be invited as an optional attendee
  - Sam will send slides to the group
  - Nelson requested that a "New business" section be added to the agenda for future meetings

## Invoice Approval

- There were no new invoices to approve.

## Adjournment

- Eric motioned to adjourn. The motion was seconded by Steve . The committee voted unanimously to adjourn at 1:47PM.

*If you would like to request a reasonable accommodation, please contact Maria Luise, ADA Compliance Coordinator at mluise@cityofmalden.org or 781-397-7000 Ext. 2005*

*For instructions on enabling live translated captions in Teams, please visit: www.cityofmalden.org/captions*
headline: Approved prior meeting minutes and reviewed cost-saving options for the Malden River Works salt shed and boathouse project.
summary: The committee approved the minutes from the 5/5/26 and 6/4/26 meetings unanimously. designLAB presented updated construction cost estimates of $4,168,600 for the salt shed and boathouse combined, along with several possible cost-saving changes such as siding, roofing, window, and conduit changes, and removing boat racks from the bid. No final decision was made on these savings options; the committee agreed to meet again on Thursday, June 25 at 2PM to continue the discussion and later send decisions to designLAB by email.
decisions: Approved the 5/5/26 and 6/4/26 meeting minutes unanimously.
Decided to meet again on Thursday, June 25 at 2PM to continue discussing cost-saving options before sending decisions to designLAB by email.
